senses.sense_definition: The surgical removal of an organ, tissue, tumor, or other body part by cutting.

examples.text: The surgeon performed a complete <w>excision</w> of the tumor to prevent the cancer from spreading.
He recovered quickly following the surgical <w>excision</w> of his infected appendix.

senses.sense_definition: The removal or cutting out of a passage, word, or section of text during editing.

examples.text: Several controversial passages were marked for <w>excision</w> before the article could be published.
The author objected strongly to the editor's sudden <w>excision</w> of the final chapter.

senses.sense_definition: The removal of a specific gene or segment of nucleic acid from a strand of genetic material.

examples.text: The cellular repair mechanism relies on nucleotide <w>excision</w> to fix DNA damaged by ultraviolet light.
Researchers achieved precise targeted <w>excision</w> of the mutated sequence using modern molecular tools.

senses.sense_definition: A property in algebraic topology stating that the relative homology groups of a topological space remain unchanged after deleting a subspace.

examples.text: The proof relies directly on the <w>excision</w> theorem to compute the relative homology groups.
In algebraic topology, <w>excision</w> allows one to simplify calculations by removing unneeded open sets.
